text.p: Following are some of the leading stories in the Swedish papers this morning. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Sweden is refusing to pay to send any more Cubans back to their homeland after being refused asylum. Sweden has paid for at least 30 in recent years. But Cuba is also refusing to foot the bill to repatriate its citizens.

- The strong rise on the Stockholm bourse so far this year means there is room for a downward move when the half year reporting season gets underway. However the paper says the market need not worry too much as the strengthen in the dollar and the pound should help give currency benefits to export companies coupled with low interest rates.

- Forestry company AssiDoman has become the main owner of Russian paper and pulp mill Segezhabumprom, buying out Daventree following months of uncertainty over the future of the project. It will oversea an investment of up to 800 million crowns in the mill and cut staff levels.
- Sales of a new low alcohol beer, folkol, with 2.8 percent alcohol, have risen about four percent in the first six months of this year, according to figures from Sweden's brewers association.

- An new type of alcohol lock, to be installed in cars of people caught drink driving, does not work in Sweden's cold climate, a study has found. The government had proposed trialling the alcohol lock from next year. A driver would have to blow into the device to prove he or she had not been drinking before the car would start.
- Forestry company AssiDoman strengthens its ownership in the troubled Russian paper mill Segezhabumprom after a four month halt in production.

- Health care product company Getinge reported a pre-tax profit of 265.6 million crowns for the first six months fo 1997 compared to 238 million crowns a year ago. Market expectations were for a profit of 265 million crowns.
- Only published on Friday during the summer.
